transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi, thank you. Um, well, what made me come in is that... after work or my classes, I'll sit down with my laptop and I just end up eating a really large amount of food. Like, I'll get a whole takeout meal, and then I'll eat that, plus chips, sweets, and basically whatever snacks I have in my desk drawer. It's just way more than I ever plan to eat when I sit down, and definitely a lot more than I would ever eat if anyone else was around.
After these episodes of eating, do you do anything to try to prevent weight gain or compensate for the food you ate?

No, I don't. Um, I don't throw up or take anything like that, if that's what you mean. I usually just... I just sit there feeling really uncomfortably full and upset with myself. But I don't do anything to actually try and undo it or burn it off.
During these times when you are eating, do you feel a sense of loss of control, like you cannot stop or control how much you are eating?

Yeah, I definitely do. It's... well, once I start, it really feels like I'm just watching myself keep reaching for the next thing. Even while I'm doing it, I'm in my head thinking, Jaime, stop, you have a budget report to finish, and I know I'm not even enjoying the food anymore at that point. But I just can't seem to make myself stop.
On average, how many times a week do these eating episodes happen?

Well, I actually... I looked back through my journal and my food delivery charges recently to try and figure that out. It seems like they've been happening most weeks ever since the restructuring started at my job. I'd say it's usually more than once a week, so it's definitely not just a random thing happening here and there.
For about how many months has this pattern of eating been happening?
It's been about four months now. It basically started right around the time the office restructuring happened and I had to start dealing with all these late-night reporting deadlines.

inference_history.note: Patient describes recurrent episodes of eating unusually large quantities of food in secret, raising differential for eating disorders characterized by binge eating, including Bulimia nervosa and Binge eating disorder.
Ruled out F50.2 (Bulimia nervosa) due to the absence of compensatory behaviors following binge eating episodes.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets diagnostic criteria for binge eating disorder (classified under F50.8 in ICD-10). Symptoms include recurrent episodes of eating objectively large quantities of food accompanied by a definitive sense of loss of control, eating alone due to embarrassment, and feeling uncomfortably full and disgusted/upset with oneself afterward. Episodes occur more than once weekly for approximately four months, with an explicit absence of recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors.

confirmed_symptoms: Eating an objectively large amount of food within a discrete period
Sense of lack of control over eating during the episode
Eating alone due to embarrassment over quantity consumed
Feeling upset with oneself and distressed after overeating
Absence of regular inappropriate compensatory behaviors (no purging, laxatives, or compensatory fasting/exercise)
